summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Alpine Linux, installs Docker inside it, and then sets up a non-root user account with a home directory and proper permissions. The user's ID, group ID, and username are configurable at build time through ARG variables, with defaults provided.

explanations.1: This special syntax declaration tells Docker to use the BuildKit parser, which supports more advanced Dockerfile features.
explanations.5: ARG defines a variable that can be passed when building the image with --build-arg; this one sets the default group ID to 1000.
explanations.9: FROM specifies the base image we're starting from — Alpine is a very small Linux distribution, useful for keeping container size down.
explanations.11: hadolint is a linter for Dockerfiles; this comment tells it to ignore a specific warning about the next line.
explanations.12: This comment explains that docker.io should be used instead of docker for non-Alpine images that use apt-get instead of apk.
explanations.15: These ARG lines re-declare the variables so they're available in later build stages; they're needed again because ARG scope resets after FROM.
explanations.19: set -e -x makes the shell exit immediately if any command fails (-e) and print each command before running it (-x), useful for debugging.
explanations.21: addgroup creates a user group with the specified group ID and name.
explanations.23: adduser creates a non-root user account with the flags -S (system user) -D (no password) -u (user ID) -G (group) -h (home directory).
explanations.25: chown recursively changes ownership of the home directory so the new user owns their own files.
explanations.27: USER switches the container to run as this non-root user for all subsequent commands and when the container runs.
